## 戰火再起擾動能源前景，長天期美債走弱

美國與伊朗互相攻擊後，長天期美債下跌，回吐部分週五曲線趨平幅度，短端卻未續跌。2年期殖利率維持4.34%，10年期上升2個基點至4.75%，創2025年1月以來高點，30年期升3個基點至5.25%。2s10s擴大至41個基點，2s30s擴大至91。

戰事威脅荷姆茲航運恢復的期待，WTI大漲3.55%至$86.36。不過，利率變化並非單純反映長期通膨預期升高：10年期實質殖利率上升2個基點至2.44%，解釋全數名目漲幅，損益兩平通膨率仍為2.31%。布蘭特也與WTI分歧，下跌0.81%至$88.59。

股市由半導體領跌，指數跌幅2.92%；S&P 500下跌0.58%，Nasdaq 100跌0.62%，美元上漲0.26%。投資級債券部位下跌0.49%，主要高收益債ETF僅跌約0.07%。黃金上漲0.44%，全月漲幅達11.09%。較高實質殖利率壓抑長存續期間資產，投資人對政治及地緣不確定性的避險需求卻仍在。

當日調整後，10年期殖利率8月仍持平，30年期全月仍低2個基點。財政部回購對月內表現提供支持，但戰事重啟及9月企業供給又壓抑長端。海外方面，印度強勁GDP提高緊縮預期，哥倫比亞宣布更多借款，公用事業與銀行資本工具則因具體法律進展重新定價。

## 月底交易未能支撐長債

美軍攻擊荷姆茲海峽一座島嶼，伊朗隨後對阿聯酋及約旦發動報復攻擊，川普又在美國交易時段威脅進一步行動。這是約一個月來首次直接交火，使先前航運協商之後稍微淡化的實體供應與運輸成本風險，重新受到關注。

5年期殖利率上升1個基點至4.49%，介於持平的2年期與較弱長端之間。週線仍保留上週五短端領跌的痕跡：2年期上升10個基點，10年期升5個基點，30年期升2個基點。週一改變的是賣壓分布，並未形成另一套明確的9月政策利率預測。

紐約時間下午4點指數再平衡前後，一分鐘內約24.4萬口12月10年期公債期貨成交，接近全天成交量10%，長債卻未獲明顯收盤支撐。投資人另花約$650萬買進12月長債賣權，對應11月20日到期時30年期殖利率約5.7%的情境。這是防範更深跌勢的部位，不能直接當成買方對殖利率的預測。

Bessent為擴大回購辯護，表示要減緩市場單向交易，沒有干預，美債表現可能更差。他援引的比較是，美國10年期8月僅升約2個基點，德國超過10個基點，日本超過15個基點。不過，原先承諾提出的財政整頓說明，被延後到未來數週或數月；回購支持交易條件之際，財政細節反而更不急於揭曉。

美元當日小漲後，8月仍下跌0.38%，顯示較高實質殖利率並未轉化為整月單向的匯率支持。投資人同時面對聯準會更堅定的抗通膨立場，以及能源、財政計畫與政府介入債市規模等未解問題。

## 印度成長超預期，日本殖利率吸引國內資金關注

印度4至6月GDP年增7.8%，高於市場中位預估7.3%及印度央行估計7%；前季由7.8%上修至8.6%，為現行數列最高。製造業增速從8.3%升至9.2%，金融服務從8.8%升至12.1%，固定投資從5.8%升至11.9%，民間消費從6.8%升至7.1%。公布後10年期公債殖利率上升4個基點至6.95%。

央行8月維持利率5.25%後，強勁活動增加其回應物價的空間。一名民間經濟學家主張會計年度下半年可升50個基點，首席經濟顧問V. Anantha Nageswaran則強調，通膨仍在2%至6%容許區間，官員正觀察第二輪效應。印度近90%原油仰賴進口，因此即使國內成長強，油價再漲仍可能推高物價、壓縮消費及企業利潤。

德國8月通膨則沒有預期嚴重，年增2.9%，高於前期2.8%、為4月以來最快，但低於預估3.1%。能源加速，服務與食品通膨卻降溫。這支持歐洲央行在存款利率2.25%的基礎上，採取市場預期的9月升息，尚未證明需要一連串持續調升。

日本收到更直接的美方訊息。依美國官員對會面的說明，Bessent告訴片山皋月與植田和男，日本下一步應升息。日圓收在每美元約159.69，當日僅升0.3%，7月干預帶來的漲幅已回吐過半。這比先前只期待日本適當行動更明確，但不是日本央行的決策。

10年期日債殖利率觸及2.95%，為1996年以來最高。分析師開始認為，GPIF未來可能將國內債券目標從25%提高至30%至35%。以¥318兆資產計算，每調整1個百分點即超過¥3兆；一項估算認為，配置30%可能帶來約¥16兆日圓買盤，35%則約¥32兆。GPIF在4至6月已買入¥5.7兆日本債券，為至少2020會計年度以來最大單季金額。

基金並未宣布更改目標，並表示目前環境與五年投資組合原先假設沒有重大差異。批評者也指出，增加債券可能迫使其他部位承擔更多風險，才能達到長期報酬高於名目工資成長1.9個百分點的目標。較高殖利率使國內債券更有吸引力，但未來配置可能調整，不等於下一場標售立即獲得保證需求。

紐西蘭受訪21名經濟學家全數預期，央行週三升息25個基點至2.75%，連續第二次調升。第2季通膨4.1%，超過1%至3%目標，即使經濟可能萎縮、失業率達十一年高點5.6%。這項預測反映的是避免燃料及其他供應成本延續至復甦期的考量，不代表目前景氣強勁。

## 哥倫比亞增加供給，高殖利率改變拉美資金配置

哥倫比亞告知交易商，計畫在2026年增加約$110億融資並進行債務交換，其中逾$30億來自海外、主要透過債券，約COP25兆來自國內。先前揭露2027年赤字預估占GDP 9.4%，已使週五10年期本地殖利率上升逾30個基點，披索最多貶2.1%；週一殖利率與交換利率續升，披索再跌0.9%，為新興市場最弱。

本地債今年仍上漲29%、領先新興市場，但新增供給挑戰了原先的高息交易。BTG Pactual預期曲線中段與長端調整最大。財長Miguel Gómez計畫9月7日當週到紐約與華盛頓會晤，並否認尋求IMF救援。多邊融資或可信的財政整頓法可降低發債依賴，眼前標售則將顯示買方需要多少讓利。

沙烏地阿拉伯正初步討論至少$80億貸款，沙烏地阿美也另與銀行洽談，兩案皆未定。伊朗衝突干擾貿易及區域供應鏈時，替代管道能降低對單一債市窗口的依賴，但同樣會占用基建及科技借款人爭取的銀行額度。

巴西高固定收益報酬，正改變資產管理產業的控制權。Arminio Fraga認為，雙位數債券收益使獨立避險基金難以留住資金，因此同意將Gavea Investimentos基金轉予Bradesco。七家大型獨立機構的境內總經基金資產，自2022年以來近乎減半至約R$890億；整體避險基金業同期流出R$6,720億。大型金融機構內部的總經基金卻自2019年以來近乎倍增至R$5,420億。交易員預期至少到2027年底，政策利率仍高於13%，使公債及稅務優惠公司債持續成為吸收儲蓄的強勁對手。

智利投資人則更願意承擔企業信用風險。24名受訪分析師及交易員中，17%願意在9月持有最低BBB債券，比前月占比高逾三倍，也是3月以來最高；另26%可接受A、26%偏好AA以上，30%仍選最高評級。降低企業稅及行政障礙的法案預計9月上半月成法，3月以來近$180億專案已獲環評批准，預算機關預估明年成長3.7%。

但財政代價仍不可忽視。智利第1季萎縮0.3%後，第2季停滯；改革預計至少五年減少政府收入，總債務又朝GDP 45%靠近，一些分析師認為這可能帶來降評風險。企業債樂觀情緒部分取決於成長能否及時到來，抵銷稅收損失。

## 公用事業利差走寬，CDK與瑞銀推進具體債權條款

加州議員未納入原先提議的野火求償保護，使PG&E的6.3% 2056年券利差走寬15個基點至138，Edison International的4% 2047年券走寬10個基點至133。州長Newsom原想阻止保險公司向公用事業代位求償，但週六法案沒有這項保護，公司仍面對未來索賠，市場也擔心降評。

法案仍擬禁止保險公司將公用事業求償權出售給投資人、限制重大火災責任企業執行長獎金、加快受災者付款並加強預防。這些改變影響求償程序，卻沒有替債券持有人原本希望降低的資產負債表曝險設上限。表決預計週二進行。

CDK Global與債權人協商委員會達成重整協議，將股東持有債權往後順位移，並展延擔保債期限。Brookfield Business Partners擬將約$6.75億部位換成較低順位、以債付息的PIK債；委員會貸款人則將2029年擔保債權，以8%折價換成兩年半後到期的新債。2024年網攻後的獲利及再融資困難，使CDK近$40億2029年定期貸款週五僅約52美分。

如果Brookfield在交割前繼續買債，折價可能增至13%，回購上限約$12億。其他貸款人可協商，但待遇不能優於委員會；合作協議也禁止參與者退出、另談交易。穆迪8月初已將CDK降兩級至Caa2，如今協議新增的是具體順位、展延與減記分配，而不只是再次指出已知困境。

瑞士上院經濟委員會以10票對2票、1票棄權，建議重新設計的AT1可支應瑞銀海外子公司約$200億新增資本要求的至多50%，其餘由股本支應。瑞銀約占€2,860億歐洲AT1市場7%，其未來發行及條款對整個資產類別都有影響。

建議架構下，普通股資本低於最低要求時，將停止股利、股票回購及AT1息票，並縮減獎金池，讓債務在處置前就吸收損失，也降低全數使用普通股的成本。不過，這仍是階段性政治建議：上院將在9月14日至10月2日會期表決，較偏左的下院可能推翻讓步。財政部仍質疑AT1在危機中的可靠性，社會民主黨也批評該建議。

## 亞洲資料中心借款逼近銀行產業額度

亞洲資料中心貸款自2025年初以來接近$290億，今年已達創紀錄的$150億，比同期快27%。DayOne正討論將既有額度擴大至$70億，若成案將是區域最大資料中心融資。銀行人士表示，貸款機構正接近產業限額，開始更挑選股東、報酬及風險移轉方式。

法國農業信貸尋求出售部分香港資料中心貸款，摩根士丹利也研究重大風險移轉交易以避險。銀行愈來愈需要釋放資本，才能承作下一案；ABS與專案債提供可能出口。美國光纖及資料中心業主去年發行約$230億資產證券化債務，增加86%。

Nvidia透過可轉債投資聯發科$35億，是其美國以外最大直接投資，也配合雙方把加速運算延伸至客製化系統的合作。聯發科取得期限資金，Nvidia可參與股權價值，資金來源因而不同於銀行貸款或無擔保發債。

專案執行同樣受限。美國科技公司今年規畫逾$7,000億AI基建支出，但2026年前三個月至少75案、約$1,300億，因地方反對而遭阻擋或延後。8月調查顯示61%成年人反對在住家附近新建資料中心，比2至3月調查多12個百分點。紐約已暫停超大型設施，德州新開發也實質凍結。設備債、租約及未來容量融資所依賴的營運資產，可能因許可、電力與社區接受度而延後成形。

## 下一交易日先看美國數據與日本標售

9月1日紐約時間上午9:45公布8月S&P製造業PMI終值，10點接著公布ISM製造業、7月職缺及建築支出。ISM預估55.2，職缺估730萬；訂單、就業及價格可協助分辨需求是否持續，或只是月底前已見轉弱。週五非農及9月11日CPI，再決定傑克森洞後市場推估的利率路徑能否維持。

日本10年期標售在週二東京時間12:35，殖利率接近3%。前次投標倍數2.56，為2025年5月以來最弱，近期2年期標售也已顯示投資人在9月17至18日央行會議前較謹慎。這將檢驗即使GPIF不改目標，目前收益是否足以吸引國內買方。紐西蘭週三預期升至2.75%，則另行檢驗央行在弱景氣中收緊政策的意願。

加州週二表決將決定公用事業責任條款，哥倫比亞標售及9月財長會晤將釐清COP25兆本地、逾$30億海外融資的承接。DayOne最終貸款條件也仍開放，包括銀行能否在不犧牲定價或保障下，分銷另一筆創紀錄額度。

overall_summary.headline: 戰火再起壓抑長債，加州野火法案使公用事業利差走寬
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美伊再度交火後，WTI大漲3.55%，布蘭特卻跌0.81%。10年期損益兩平通膨率維持2.31%，實質殖利率升至2.44%。月底期貨交易未能支撐長債，曲線在週五短端領跌後轉陡。

印度成長7.8%，強化日後升息理由。日本殖利率接近3%，帶動對GPIF潛在需求的討論，但基金並未宣布調整配置。哥倫比亞增加$110億融資計畫，推升本地殖利率、壓低披索。

加州法案缺少原先期待的代位求償保護；CDK議定股東債權次順位化及交換條件，瑞士委員會則支持AT1支應瑞銀額外資本要求的至多一半。亞洲資料中心貸款逼近銀行集中限額，推動風險移轉及更多籌資管道。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Long Treasuries weaken as renewed fighting unsettles the energy outlook

Long Treasuries fell as the US and Iran exchanged attacks, reversing some of Friday's curve flattening without adding to the front-end selloff. The 2-year held at 4.34%, while the 10-year rose 2 basis points to 4.75%, its highest since January 2025, and the 30-year added 3 to 5.25%. Two-to-10-year spreads widened to 41 basis points and 2s30s to 91.

WTI jumped 3.55% to $86.36 as the fighting threatened hopes of normalizing Hormuz traffic. The rates response was not a simple rise in long-term inflation expectations: 10-year real yields increased 2 basis points to 2.44%, accounting for the full nominal move, while breakevens stayed at 2.31%. Brent also diverged from WTI, falling 0.81% to $88.59.

Equities declined, led by semiconductors' 2.92% loss. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.62% and the dollar gained 0.26%. Investment-grade bond exposure fell 0.49%, while the principal high-yield funds lost only about 0.07%. Gold rose 0.44%, bringing its monthly gain to 11.09%. Higher real yields pressured duration, but demand for protection from political and geopolitical uncertainty persisted.

The latest move left the 10-year yield unchanged for August and the 30-year 2 basis points lower. Treasury buybacks still provided support over the month, even as renewed fighting and September corporate supply weighed on the long end. Elsewhere, India's strong GDP raised tightening expectations, Colombia announced more borrowing, and specific legal decisions moved utility and bank-capital risk.

## Month-end trading offers little help to long bonds

American forces struck an island in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran retaliated with attacks directed at the UAE and Jordan. Trump threatened further action during the US session. The first direct exchange in about a month brought physical disruption and transport costs back into focus after the earlier shipping negotiations.

Five-year yields rose 1 basis point to 4.49%, between an unchanged 2-year and the weaker long end. The weekly comparison still reflected Friday's front-end-led move: 2-year yields were up 10 basis points, versus 5 at ten years and 2 at thirty. Monday changed that day's distribution of selling rather than establishing a new September policy-rate forecast.

Nearly 244,000 December 10-year note futures traded within one minute around the 4 p.m. New York index rebalance, close to 10% of daily volume, yet long bonds received little closing support. Investors also spent roughly $6.5 million on December Treasury-bond puts associated with a 30-year yield near 5.7% at their November 20 expiry. The purchase was protection against a deeper decline, not proof that the buyer expected that yield.

Bessent defended expanded buybacks as a way to slow one-way trading and argued that Treasuries might otherwise have performed worse. In his comparison, the US 10-year had risen only about 2 basis points in August, against more than 10 in Germany and 15 in Japan. He also pushed a promised fiscal-consolidation presentation back to the coming weeks or months, leaving detail less immediate even as repurchases supported trading conditions.

The dollar's modest daily rise still left it 0.38% lower over August. Higher real yields had not produced an unqualified currency gain over the month. Investors continued to face both a firmer Fed inflation stance and unresolved questions over energy, fiscal plans and the scale of official intervention in the bond market.

## Indian growth surprises; Japanese yields draw attention from domestic investors

India's April–June GDP grew 7.8% year over year, above the 7.3% median forecast and the RBI's 7% estimate. The prior quarter was revised to 8.6% from 7.8%, the highest in the current series. Manufacturing accelerated to 9.2% from 8.3%, financial services to 12.1% from 8.8%, fixed investment to 11.9% from 5.8%, and private consumption to 7.1% from 6.8%. Ten-year government yields rose 4 basis points to 6.95% after the release.

Stronger activity gave the RBI more room to respond to prices after holding at 5.25% in August. One private-sector economist argued for 50 basis points of tightening in the fiscal year's second half. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran instead emphasized that inflation remained within the 2%–6% tolerance band and officials were monitoring second-round effects. India imports nearly 90% of its crude; renewed oil pressure can raise inflation while squeezing consumers and company margins even when domestic growth is strong.

Germany's August inflation was less severe than expected. Prices rose 2.9%, up from 2.8% and the strongest since April, but below the 3.1% forecast. Energy accelerated while services and food inflation eased. The release supported the expected September ECB step from a 2.25% deposit rate without establishing that a long sequence of hikes was necessary.

Japan received a more direct US message. According to a US official's account, Bessent told Satsuki Katayama and Kazuo Ueda that Japan's next step should be a rate increase. The yen ended near 159.69 per dollar, only 0.3% stronger on the day and having surrendered more than half the gains from July intervention. The statement went beyond his earlier expectation that Japan would act appropriately, but it was not a BOJ decision.

Ten-year JGB yields touched 2.95%, their highest since 1996. Analysts argued that GPIF could eventually lift its domestic-bond target from 25% to 30%–35%. On assets of ¥318 trillion, one percentage point represents more than ¥3 trillion; an estimate put yen purchases associated with a 30% allocation near ¥16 trillion and a 35% allocation near ¥32 trillion. GPIF had already bought ¥5.7 trillion of Japanese debt in April–June, its largest quarter since at least fiscal 2020.

The fund has not announced such a target change. It said conditions were not materially different from assumptions underlying its five-year portfolio. Critics also noted that more bonds could require greater risk elsewhere to meet its objective of earning 1.9 percentage points above nominal wage growth over the long run. Higher yields make domestic bonds more attractive, but prospective allocation changes do not guarantee immediate demand at the next auction.

All 21 economists surveyed expected New Zealand to raise its cash rate 25 basis points to 2.75% on Wednesday, a second consecutive increase. Q2 inflation reached 4.1%, above the 1%–3% target, even though the economy may have contracted and unemployment hit an 11-year high of 5.6%. The forecast reflects concern that fuel and other supply costs could persist into a recovery, not evidence of strong current activity.

## Colombia adds supply while high yields reshape Latin American portfolios

Colombia told market makers it planned about $11 billion of additional 2026 financing and debt swaps. More than $3 billion would come from overseas, mainly bonds, and about 25 trillion pesos from the local market. This followed the previously disclosed 2027 deficit estimate of 9.4% of GDP, which had pushed 10-year local yields up more than 30 basis points and weakened the peso as much as 2.1% on Friday. Yields and swaps rose again Monday; the peso fell another 0.9%, the worst performance among emerging-market currencies.

Local bonds remained up 29% this year, leading emerging-market peers, but added supply challenged the carry trade. BTG Pactual expected the belly and long end to adjust most. Finance Minister Miguel Gómez plans New York and Washington meetings in the week of September 7 while rejecting suggestions of an IMF rescue. Multilateral funding or a credible consolidation law could reduce reliance on bond sales; upcoming auctions will show the concessions buyers require in the meantime.

Saudi Arabia is in early talks for a loan of at least $8 billion, with Aramco separately discussing funding with banks. Neither deal is final. The alternatives could reduce dependence on one bond-market window as the Iran conflict disrupts trade and regional supply chains, but would use bank capacity also sought by infrastructure and technology borrowers.

In Brazil, high fixed-income returns are changing the ownership of fund management. Arminio Fraga agreed to transfer Gavea Investimentos' funds to Bradesco after concluding that double-digit bond returns made retaining assets difficult for an independent hedge fund. Seven large independent firms' onshore macro assets have nearly halved since 2022 to around 89 billion reais. The wider hedge-fund industry has lost 672 billion reais over that period, while macro funds inside large financial institutions nearly doubled since 2019 to 542 billion. Traders expected policy rates above 13% through at least end-2027, leaving government and tax-advantaged corporate bonds strong competitors for savings.

Chilean investors were more willing to take corporate risk. Of 24 surveyed analysts and traders, 17% would own BBB bonds in September, over three times the prior month's share and the most since March. Another 26% would go to A, 26% preferred AA or above, and 30% stayed in the highest ratings. A bill reducing corporate taxes and administrative barriers was expected to become law in the first half of September; almost $18 billion of projects had received environmental approval since March, and the budget office forecast 3.7% growth next year.

The fiscal cost remained relevant. Chile stagnated in Q2 after a 0.3% Q1 contraction, the reform was expected to reduce revenue for at least five years, and gross debt was moving toward 45% of GDP, a level some analysts associated with downgrade risk. The credit optimism depends in part on growth arriving quickly enough to offset that loss of revenue.

## Utility spreads widen; CDK and UBS advance specific creditor terms

PG&E's 6.3% 2056 bond spread widened 15 basis points to 138 and Edison International's 4% 2047 notes widened 10 to 133 after California lawmakers omitted a proposed shield from wildfire claims. Newsom had wanted to prevent insurers from pursuing utilities through subrogation. Saturday's bill did not include that protection, leaving companies exposed to future claims and raising downgrade concerns.

The bill would still bar insurers from selling utility claims to investors, restrict chief-executive bonuses at utilities liable for catastrophic fires, speed survivor payments and increase prevention. Those changes affect the claims process but do not cap the balance-sheet exposure bondholders had hoped to reduce. A vote was expected Tuesday.

CDK Global agreed with a creditor steering committee on a restructuring that would subordinate sponsor holdings and extend secured maturities. Brookfield Business Partners would exchange about $675 million into lower-ranking payment-in-kind paper. Committee lenders would exchange 2029 secured obligations for debt due two-and-a-half years later at an 8% discount. CDK's nearly $4 billion 2029 term loan traded near 52 cents Friday after earnings and refinancing difficulties following the 2024 cyberattack.

The discount could increase to 13% if Brookfield keeps purchasing debt before closing, with repurchases capped near $1.2 billion. Other lenders can negotiate, but cannot receive better treatment than the committee; a cooperation agreement prevents participating holders from leaving for a separate deal. Moody's had cut CDK two notches to Caa2 in early August. The current agreement adds specific ranking, extension and haircut terms to that already-known distress.

Switzerland's upper-house economic committee voted 10–2, with one abstention, to let redesigned AT1 cover as much as 50% of UBS's roughly $20 billion additional capital requirement for foreign subsidiaries. Equity would cover the rest. UBS's approximately 7% share of the €286 billion European AT1 market makes its future issuance and terms material to the broader asset class.

Under the recommended framework, breaching minimum common-equity requirements would halt dividends, buybacks and AT1 coupons and reduce the bonus pool. The proposal aims to make debt absorb losses before resolution, lowering UBS's cost relative to an all-equity requirement. It remains an interim political recommendation: the upper house votes in its September 14–October 2 session, and the more left-leaning lower house could reverse concessions. The Finance Ministry still questions AT1's reliability in a crisis, and the Social Democrats criticized the recommendation.

## Asian data-center lending approaches bank concentration limits

Asian data-center loans have reached nearly $29 billion since the start of 2025, including a record $15 billion this year, 27% ahead of the comparable period. DayOne is discussing expanding a facility to as much as $7 billion, which would be the region's largest data-center financing. Bankers said lenders were approaching sector limits and becoming more selective about sponsors, returns and risk transfer.

Credit Agricole sought to sell part of a Hong Kong data-center loan, and Morgan Stanley explored significant-risk transfer to hedge exposure. Banks increasingly need to recycle capital before underwriting further projects. ABS and project bonds offer potential outlets: US fiber and data-center owners issued about $23 billion of asset-backed debt last year, up 86%.

Nvidia's $3.5 billion MediaTek investment through convertible bonds brought strategic capital into another part of the market. Its largest direct investment outside the US accompanies a partnership to extend accelerated computing into customized systems. MediaTek receives term funding while Nvidia can participate in equity value, a different source of capital from bank loans or unsecured issuance.

Execution is also constraining projects. US technology companies plan over $700 billion of AI infrastructure spending this year, but local opposition blocked or delayed at least 75 projects worth about $130 billion in the first three months of 2026. An August survey found 61% of adults opposed a new data center locally, 12 percentage points more than in February–March surveys. New York imposed a hyperscale moratorium, while Texas had an effective development freeze. Permits, power and community acceptance can delay the operating asset on which equipment debt, leases and future-capacity financing depend.

## US releases and Japan's auction lead the next session

Final August S&P manufacturing PMI arrives September 1 at 9:45 a.m. New York time, followed at 10 a.m. by ISM manufacturing, July job openings and construction spending. ISM consensus is 55.2 and vacancies are estimated at 7.3 million. Orders, employment and prices will help distinguish durable demand from the weaker readings seen before month-end. Friday's payroll report and September 11 CPI then inform whether the rate path inferred after Jackson Hole holds.

Japan's 10-year auction is due Tuesday at 12:35 p.m. Tokyo time, with yields near 3%. The prior sale's 2.56 bid-to-cover ratio was the weakest since May 2025, and the recent 2-year auction already showed caution before the September 17–18 BOJ meeting. Demand will test whether current yields attract domestic buyers without a GPIF target change. New Zealand's expected Wednesday increase to 2.75% is a separate test of tightening through weak activity.

California's Tuesday vote will determine the utility liability provisions. Colombia's auctions and September ministerial meetings will clarify placement of 25 trillion pesos locally and more than $3 billion abroad. DayOne's final loan terms remain open, including whether banks can distribute another record facility without sacrificing price or protections.
